utterances.text: As Exhibit P6321, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And if we could go back now to page 118 in the B/C/S and figure 65 that's on that page.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And this relates to paragraph 81 of your report. Now, at paragraph 81 in about the third paragraph, and this is the bottom of page 63 in the English, you state that there was a shell that you claim exploded at the edge of the playground and this disturbed the soil between the playground and the footpath. And then you state: "The blast from the shell that exploded subsequently on the footpath threw the loose soil for the most part in the direction of its approach, hence the substantial soil traces on the playground." And if we could just zoom in on figure 65, please. This is the figure where you say there is a substantial soil trace on the playground. And you say figure 65 shows the soil traces which are almost at the square angle in relation to the edge of the playground and this shows that the shell had come in at an azimuth of 220 to 230 degrees. So if I understand you correctly, the shell that landed on the footpath, the one that was examined by the investigators, it's your view that that shell flew in essentially over the playground from roughly the south-west and then hit the footpath and that caused the soil to be strewn onto the playground. Do I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you have understood me correctly. The traces of soil on the footpath represent the incoming trajectory of the shell. This is not on the footpath, I apologise, on the playground. The traces of soil that we can see on the playground, this is the playground, and on it we can see that there are traces of soil. That is the consequence of the landing of the shell which we saw previously which fell at the edge of the concrete footpath. And the soil which was disturbed by the blast by the previous shell was thrown along its incoming trajectory by the next shell. This shell has not been examined in the documents at all, but it is marked as you can see both with a red arrow and a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. So it's on this basis you conclude that the shell that landed on the footpath, it had a trajectory of 220 to 230 degrees roughly south-west; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me just check if I mention that direction and if you now read out the direction that I marked, but that is certainly the direction along which the disturbed soil stretches.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. I'm looking at page --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. I agree, 220 to 230, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. If we could now go to page 134 of the B/C/S and figure 81. And this relates to paragraph 87 of your report and the English page reference is page 70. And if we could zoom in on the photograph here. Now, this is again the photograph taken at the time of the shell that hit the edge of the footpath which you just confirmed that you had concluded that it flew in over the playground from a south-westerly direction. Now, here you have examined the shrapnel pattern on the photograph and you conclude that the shell -- the trajectory of the shell is reflected in the line number 1, which you stated the incoming direction of the shell determined on the basis of the shrapnel pattern on the asphalt surface.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, if we go to page -- sorry, the next page in the B/C/S, you have depicted that direction in figure 82 and it is -- you say that the incoming angle is about 240 degrees, but we can see that what you say the incoming angle is based on your crater analysis it's a direction coming in from roughly the north-east. And the reason you get the measurement of 239 degrees is because you've measured from north all the way around to essentially the opposite direction from where you allege the shell was fired from. So I'm going to put it to you that what you -- the calculation -- the determination you made on the basis of the crater analysis you did on the photograph in figure 81, if we could just go back to page 134, that's line 1, that is essentially a north-easterly direction coming in across the footpath. Whereas previously you had said because of the soil pattern on the playground, the shell flew in over the playground from a south-westerly direction and hit the footpath. So you've come up with two totally different trajectories for the same shell in these two different parts of your report; right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we ask Ms. Gustafson to tell us where the north is here. How do we determine the position of the north in photographs?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I think the question is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For me I don't follow, but I'm confident that Ms. Subotic is capable of answering the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me start from some place so that we can try to unravel this. In image 82, figure 82, shows two trajectories. One trajectory is the incoming trajectory of the shell as determined by the investigation organs and that is practically the east. And it is marked by number 1 in relation to the incident. The other trajectory represents the boundary azimuth between the BH army positions and the VRS positions. To the left is the BH army and to the right is the VRS. So 239, the azimuth which is here, was not the result of any calculations but is a possible tangential line of the separation line. I mean, that is the most approximate tangential line in relation to the separation line. And next, in figure 81 it was assessed that the angle of descent is about 60 degrees in relation to the curb in this photograph, and the curb was determined as it can be seen before that on Google Earth with the azimuth of 300 degrees. What follows from that is that the azimuth of the incoming trajectory is around, it does not say exactly, but approximately around 240. And the trajectory that we mentioned earlier on was between 220 and 230. So I don't see any inconsistencies here.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Let me put it in another way. You agree that the -- when you look at figure 81, look at the photo in figure 81, the playground is on the side where the photograph is being taken from; right? Yes. It's parallel to the footpath and in the direction from where the photograph -- photographer appears to be standing when taking this picture; right? I see you nodding. Can you just agree verbally.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The playground theoretically speaking is at an angle and this -- the photograph was made from the direction of the playground, that is to say behind the back of the person who made a photograph is the position where the playground is located. This is what you're asking me; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Now, a few moments ago when we looked at the photo that had the soil on it, you agreed that the shell flew in over the playground and hit the footpath and that caused the soil to be expelled onto the playground, whereas here with your line number 1, you're stating that the shell in fact flew in from a different direction, essentially across the footpath from the other side and hit the footpath. And those two are inconsistent. That's what I'm putting to you.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to read that where I wrote the one and the other because I think some sort of confusion follows from that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, you make the first conclusion in paragraph 81 in about the third paragraph -- or sorry, paragraph 81 in about the third paragraph of that numbered paragraph. And perhaps we could go back to figure 65 which shows the soil.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this third paragraph it reads that soil traces which are almost at a square angle in relation to the edge of the playground or the curb that can be seen on the photograph shows that the shell had come in at an azimuth of 220 or 230 degrees and perhaps even smaller which is contrary to the azimuth determined by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes, and you confirmed that based on this figure 65 that that implied that the shell flew in essentially over the playground from a south-westerly direction, namely 220 to 230 degrees. But when you did your crater analysis --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Flew in with an azimuth -- at an azimuth of 220 or 230 degrees or even smaller.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Right. And then when you did your crater analysis you reached a very different conclusion, namely, that the shell flew in over the footpath, although at an angle, and hit the footpath.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look. I wrote in one place and in the other that the angles are between 220 and 240. What you are saying now is not mentioned anywhere or I cannot find it that I wrote that. In both sections, we are talking about this range of azimuths. I don't know where you found that I said across the playground. I have read now what you told me and it says there precisely that the trajectory was 220 to 230, and by the analysis of the photograph we determined that it was around 240. So you will allow that with the precision of all the methods this is just a general conclusion. This is why we said around 240, but these are the trajectories.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: To be clear, shall we ask Ms. Subotic to mark the direction of projectile on figure 65, if that helps you?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That may. If we could --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: -- blow up figure 65.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh. For example -- but no, let's erase this. So we wouldn't have ... As this was fire at an area, do not take it literally but that is an approximation. The trajectory in relation to the playground as far as we can see it now. However, the analysis of the traces on the footpath which we saw in figure 67 or 8, I think, we could see there that it was at an angle of around 240, the azimuth of around 240. So this is the incoming trajectory of the shell which landed on the footpath. And these are the traces of the soil spreading in this direction -- no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Date and signature, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I think I entered yesterday's date. Today's the 16th; correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit P6322.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I think that on the previous image I wrote yesterday's date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. No problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just realised.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, what you just marked is, in fact, roughly consistent with what you marked in the other photograph, but what you said when I initially asked you about this photograph is you agreed with me that the shell flew in essentially over the playground from the south-west and hit the footpath and that caused the soil to be strewn onto the playground. And you said -- you agreed with that. You said: "Yes, you have understood me correctly. The traces of the soil on the footpath" and then you corrected yourself and said "the playground represent the incoming trajectory of the shell." And that was at page 47. And now what you've drawn is something completely different; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please excuse me, but your questions are extremely long and I cannot follow the parameters that you mention. I stand by -- completely by what is included in the report, and I haven't managed to find in it what you claim we wrote. So I apologise, it's probably my mistake, but I cannot follow. The questions are so long. I cannot keep all the parameters in my head up until the moment when I'm supposed to answer. I probably answered having in mind the sequence of the shells and the effects created by the first shell that hit the curb at the edge of the playground. So I probably focused on explaining the effect and where did the soil come from and it actually is linked with the next shell that landed. I stand by fully to what I wrote here and what is included in my report. Perhaps I was inattentive and I may have said that by mistake. But I think that considering all your questions I would probably agree with the last thing that you said. I'm not blaming you. It's simply that I am unable to follow.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Could we go to page 124 of the B/C/S. And this is where you claim that the error in the crime scene sketch resulted in an erroneous determination of the incoming trajectory. And this is paragraph 83. Now, at paragraph 83, and this is at pages 64 and 65 in the English, you note that the crime scene sketch -- the direction north was marked erroneously in the crime scene sketch. And you conclude from that that the incoming direction was determined erroneously. Now, you don't explain in your report based on the evidence how the error in the sketch resulted in an error in the determination of trajectory. And the reason for that failure is because if you actually look at the evidence, the evidence clearly shows that the error in the crime scene sketch had no impact on the determination of the trajectory. So in your testimony in your examination the other day at page 38271 you said about this error: "Due to this error of 60 degrees, they drew erroneous conclusions about the direction from which the shells had arrived. I think that KDZ166, the witness, agreed with this when we presented to him the situation as depicted here." But, in fact, Witness KDZ166 said that the error in his sketch had no impact on the determination of the direction of fire. At page 8297 he was asked: "Now we have a new northerly direction, so if you change it from 90 degrees to some 30 or 40 degrees, does that affect the direction from which the shell came?" And he answered: "No, it doesn't. I did not plot the direction onto my sketch from which the shell came because that part of the work, that is, to establish the direction, was done by ballistics experts." And he went on to explain how the ballistics experts determined the direction by examining the traces of the impact on the ground. And Mr. Sabljica who testified in your presence and who was one of the ballistics experts at this incident also said that the sketch was irrelevant to determining the direction of fire: "Because what we did in our investigations had to do with the actual situation and the actual trace evidence found on site." And that's at transcript page 7800. And you also failed to mention that the investigation file states explicitly that the direction from which the shells came was established by a compass, and that's P1710, page 7. Not to mention the fact that the photographs in the investigation file show the investigators determining the direction of fire with a compass, and that's P1707. Now, Ms. Subotic, you don't mention any of this evidence, and that's a pretty misleading thing to do, to assert that the crime scene sketch error resulted in an error in determining the direction of fire without mentioning any of the evidence that demonstrates overwhelming that that is not the case; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President, I think that we have to change our method of work here in order to really be successful at this because this is an impossible question to answer if it's not broken up. There are so many elements that have been placed in this question that it's really impossible. And if she gives an answer, it could very well be incomplete or partial. So I object. I think that Ms. Gustafson -- first of all, I see what she's trying to do, she is trying to consolidate so she saves time, which I understand, but let her have as much time as she needs to test this evidence completely. But let's do it right. Let's break it up one by one and then you can get accurate answers that way. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think in this case -- this is not a fact witness. This is an expert witness who has purported to actually have evaluated all this evidence already --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I think your question is rather lengthy. I agree with that. And then whether Ms. Subotic is able to answer those lengthy questions, I'm not sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Well, as I said, Your Honour, she has purported to have examined the record. She was present when some of these witnesses testified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But could you break it down. But let's see whether --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Let me put it this way, Ms. Subotic. There is a great deal of evidence in this case that the crime scene sketch error had no impact on the determination of direction of fire. You don't mention any of that evidence in your report and that's a misleading thing to do; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that's a fair question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm afraid that I will have to start with last things first and that I will have to say the following: I say with full responsibility that in the hundreds of pages that I have authored there's no single line that would mislead any reader, including the Trial Chamber, to an erroneous conclusion. First of all, whoever looked at the crime reports cannot -- can only say [as interpreted] that a sketch is not a document based on which the technicians made their conclusion. That is not the case. In that case, the sketch is an unnecessary [Realtime transcript read in error "necessary"] document in a crime file. That would be number one. Number two, the manner in which the investigators determined the direction north and the direction of the incoming shell is unacceptable in any document, let alone the document of that kind. We saw many times that this was done by taking a map, but we can't see how the map was termed because that's the kind the photo is, and the measuring tape was placed on that and we can't see in the photo when it was that. Irrespective of the intention, all photo documents in crime files have to be clear and they can -- they have to be tested. So much about the reserve thing at the end. Second of all, we have analysed these traces in great detail here and we conclude -- we reached conclusions that are based on technical and physical evidence based on the photo documentation that was made and they were not interpreted properly. Incorrect things were noted. So let us not say that I'm trying to deceive any reader, including the Trial Chamber, because I'm insulted by that as a person and as an expert.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Transcript. [Interpretation] May I make corrections in the transcript?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On line 18 on page 57, it was incorrectly noted that "the sketch is a necessary...," the witness said "unnecessary." [In English] Number two, this line 20, is completely wrongly translated and written down, recorded. No compass mentioned and so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think Ms. Subotic would agree that it should read "unnecessary" instead of "necessary"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I was having a sip of water. I was not paying attention. Could you repeat that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I will read out the transcript as it reads. "First of all, whoever looked at the crime report can only say that sketch is not a document based on which the technicians made their conclusion. That is not the case. In that case, the sketch is a necessary document in a crime file."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So that should read as "the sketch is an unnecessary document"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No -- of course, of course. In that case it would be completely unnecessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] However, that document is one of the most elementary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you made a point, number two. Could you repeat it, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The investigators in the field determined the trajectory of the shell or its incoming direction in the following way: They placed a map on the site, on the place of the incident, and the scale of that map was 1:20.000. And then they put a compass on that map and that was their method to determine the incoming direction. This method is absolutely unacceptable. First and foremost, due to the scale of the map and also due to the incorrect method of drafting criminal and technical documentation, because neither us nor anybody else for that matter could reconstruct what they noted that they had determined based on the photos that they took. You can see a very unclear photo without any bench-marks. Those of us who are in the business, who are in the field, are aware of the basic rule. When you do an on-site investigation, you fix a point and you determine all the measures in respect of that fixed point so that you can repeat everything and you can control everything that was done because it can happen that crime technicians fails to take a measurement which needs to be taken. So whoever analyses that can go to the site and check the measurements that he wants to check. So no sketch has a fixed point in the space or on the ground. And such a sketch without a fixed point on the ground cannot be used to reconstruct the event without leading to ambiguities as to whether that had really happened. In other words, the measurement methods that were applied are unacceptable because we only see a map without any orientation with regard to a fixed point. We see a compass in the photo, but we can't see what that compass points to. Therefore, what is alleged as having been done, I don't have any doubts that it was done, but it cannot be tested. So that if something was not taken into account, it was because it could not be tested and it was not worth taking it into account. Second of all, all the physical evidence that remained on the spot - and we found them there when we got there - we tested them and they do not correspond with what the investigators claimed in their findings. I apologise, that would be that about this question that Madam Prosecutor put to me.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 57, line 16, it says [In English] "Can only." [Interpretation] I believe that "can only" should be deleted and the only thing that should remain is "cannot say." 57, 16, it's contradictory and it leads to an erroneous conclusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the context, that seems to be the case. But in the course of reviewing the transcript I think that will be checked upon. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: If we could go to page 128 in the B/C/S and look at figure 74. Ms. Subotic, this is part of your conclusions. In paragraph 68, the English page reference is page 67. Now, in this diagram you have depicted the trajectory of the shell, if the shell had flown in from the direction that the investigators established at the time, which was basically east. And you conclude that the damage on the right-hand side wall of the alcove of the building -- you note that it's significantly damaged and you conclude that the direction east is -- was erroneously determined because based on this schematic diagram this indicates that that right wall wouldn't have been so significantly damaged; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. If you look at the place where this shell landed and you can see it in the previous photo and then if you look at the distribution, the fan-like or the funnel-like distribution of fragments, it is absolutely clear that the primary blast was not on the wall which was so significantly damaged. So it could not come from that direction. It's absolutely clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And just for clarity, could you mark that right-hand side wall of the alcove that was -- where you noted the significant damage. For the parties' reference that damage is depicted in figure 76 on page 130 of the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, where would you like me to mark? Should I mark on this figure or somewhere else? This figure?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yeah --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or some other figure? I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Yes. I was referring to the -- to figure 76 in your report where you've photographed the damage, but I'd like you to mark on this figure where that wall is that is significantly damaged. If you want to refer to the photograph, that may assist.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I still don't understand which photo you wanted me to mark. Where do you want me to mark the wall which was significantly damaged? Do you want me to use this schematic diagram or perhaps the photo that we took? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably there seems to have been a translation issue. Ms. Gustafson asked you to mark on this figure, on this image.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Date and signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit P6323. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Subotic, the depiction of the shell or the shrapnel fragmentation in that schematic, just to be clear, the fragments don't just go out to the left and to the right. There is a two-dimensional schematic, but the shrapnel flies out in all directions, 360 degrees around the shell in that pattern that you've depicted in the figure in front of you; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I'm again going to suggest to you that this schematic is misleading and the reason it's misleading is because you've depicted the shell as if it's flying in straight into the wall horizontally, but we all know that mortars don't fly like that. They fly at a trajectory and they land at an angle downwards. And when this shell landed at a downwards angle of 45 degrees or greater, shrapnel, as depicted in your schematic, would have flown out of the -- what would have been the top of the shell and would have hit that wall that you've circled; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. First of all, I'm sorry that this image is not clear. Had we known that such a confusion would arise, we would have a 3-D depiction. Of course it's a schematic diagram and it must not be taken laterally. The way things are depicted, they're not depicted this way in order to confuse somebody. Let's understand one thing. This shell as described by the Prosecutor fell on the left-hand side in the angle that is depicted here and when we have such a shrapnel dispersion as described by the Prosecutor, it would be possible to end up with such significant damage on this wall. It would be impossible because most of the shrapnel would damage the left-hand side and the other side would be outside of the range of this wall. I'm not saying that it would not be damaged, but it would not be damaged to such an extent. What you're saying -- possibly the damage would be somewhere up there on the upper part of the wall and there wouldn't be so much damage. If we look at the left-hand side wall and the right-hand side wall, the damage is drastically different between the two.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, you stated in your report on the -- I'm going to move on to something else now. In your report on the Markale incidents you stated that: "It is well-known that the stabiliser penetrates the ground when it is fired with charge 3 or higher charge. When a mortar shell is fired with charge 1 or with charge 2, the stabiliser falls in the immediate vicinity of the crater or is propelled back along the approximate trajectory of the mortar shell." That's at paragraph 93 of your report. Now, it's clear in this incident that we had two embedded stabilisers, so I take it that you would agree that these shells would have to have been fired at a minimum of charge 3. Are we agreed on that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. There are in evidence already in this case three JNA 120-millimetre --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise. Let me just add something to what I said. It seems to me that in this incident there was just one shell that got embedded in the footpath, whereas the second stabiliser was not embedded in the footpath. It was found on the ground, and I believe that we concluded - because we discussed that yesterday - that that stabiliser could not be used to determine the direction, as Mr. Sabljica stated, because it is visible from the fin deformations that it was not the first place where it landed. And I have to say something else. During the investigation that you said that I did not mention, Mr. Sabljica said that he also determined directions based on the positions of the stabiliser. For the reasons aforementioned, he couldn't do it based on the position of the first stabiliser because it is obvious that that was not the first place where that stabiliser landed. And as for the second stabiliser, I discussed that at great length when I spoke about Markale 1. I explained for what reason it could not be said that the incoming direction was the same as the direction of the stabiliser that was embedded in the ground because that method is absolutely unacceptable because of the stochasticity of the air phenomenon itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I don't want to get into your conclusions of any of the Markale incidents, that's not what I'm getting at here. We're at least agreed that there was one embedded stabiliser in the footpath. I'll leave it to the Chamber to evaluate the evidence on the other one. And you're agreed that if we accept your position on the charges, that that stabiliser -- sorry, that that shell would have had to have been fired at charge 3 or higher. Now, the -- there are three 120-millimetre mortar firing tables already in evidence in this case for the M74, M75, and M52, and that's P5921, 5922, and 5923. Those firing tables indicate that the minimum firing distance for any of those mortars at charge 3 is 600 metres. And that's for the M74, and that's P5921 at page 12. So would you agree that roughly 600 metres would be the minimum firing distance for the shell for which the stabiliser ended up embedded?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I were to consult firing tables - and I don't have any reason not to believe you, I'll check later - that minimum firing distance was probably interpreted properly for charge 3. So neither you nor I analysed the descent angle because we did not have the basis for that analysis. So we cannot talk about a range without taking everything into account. I believe that you read the tables well, but before I check myself I really can't answer your question because I don't know all those charges by heart.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to page 138 in the B/C/S, and in particular figure 85. Now, this relates to your claim that there is a large N on the back of the stabiliser that landed in the footpath. And what I'd like to do, if possible, is bring up on the other half of the screen P1707 at page 5, and if that's not possible, we'll just bring it up on its own. Just to orient you, Ms. Subotic, the photo that is about to come up on the other side of the screen is a photograph taken from the photo file of this incident of the same stabiliser. And if possible, I'd like to rotate the photo on the right-hand side 90 degrees clockwise so it's oriented the same. And if we could zoom in on the stabiliser both on the right-hand side photo and on the top left photo. Now, you can see the stabiliser's oriented roughly the same way in each of these photos. Your figure 85 is based on a still from a video and, as I said, the photo on the right-hand side is a photo from the photo file. That's perfect right there. Thank you. Now, first of all, do you agree that the photograph from the photo file on the right-hand side is a clear and better quality image of the stabiliser?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? It has been blown up to such an extent just like the other one on the other side, that I am not able to say why one or the other would be clearer. But I can confirm that the two images depict the same stabiliser.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And you agree that there is no large letter N in the upper left-hand side of the stabiliser in the photograph on the right-hand side; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will agree that the photo is not clear and that we can't see that letter. I can't say that it's not there. I cannot claim explicitly that it is not there based on this photo, first and foremost, because it's the same video-clip, part of that same investigation and I don't see why they should be different. On the other hand, those markings are standard markings on the primary charge. I'm sure they are there but they can't be seen. That's what I'm sure of.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You said you cannot -- you say, "I don't see why they should be different." Well, I have a suggestion for you which is that the video still on the left-hand side is of such poor quality that whatever you think you can make out in terms of a large letter N is simply a distortion resulting from the poor quality of the video still. Would you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We took this frame from the video file. We noticed the letter N. It is discernible on the upper and the lower photo that we selected. We double-checked. I am not claiming anything. I'm just saying that it was noticed and that it was given as an observation that we arrived at. None of us claims anything, but the letter N is well visible. I don't believe it's a distortion. The stabiliser is the same, indeed. But on the right-hand side we cannot see it, but I would say that this is due to the quality of the photo. I cannot say that it doesn't exist. I can say that these are the markings on the standard shell charge and those markings denote the series, the manufacturer, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: May I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I see on my screen is a different angle than we can see up there. I can see something in the left-hand side corner, something crossed, and I can't see it on the other side. How come on the screen we can see one angle and on the display we can see a totally different angle --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, this is just commentary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree. Please continue, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions on these photos. I wonder if it would be helpful, even though these photos are both in evidence, to tender this side-by-side comparison. I think it would be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can we capture this?

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I was assuming we could, but that's a good question. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can compare it at any time.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I have about ten minutes left, Your Honours, but perhaps we better take a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we -- given the reduced lunch time we are minded to break at quarter to 1.00 and have a half an hour break.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we seem to be in agreement with Mr. Tieger that these extra sessions and reduced lunch would not really change the situation. So we propose to just stay with our same schedule for now and we'll let you know next week -- we'll let you know how exactly we've worked it out, but with a few small variables we do both agree that extra sessions would not solve the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's -- basically it's -- I'm not sure that an extra session or two won't assist in the final resolution, but it certainly is accurate to say that even the Court's very generous offer and the very generous accommodation of the personnel would not entirely solve the problem of allowing every witness to be heard, and certainly reducing the lunch break today is much more symbolic than practically helpful. So we agree with Mr. Robinson in those respects.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I also join the parties thanking the interpreters and staff for their indulgence. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that we can save this image and admit it as a separate Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6324, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Subotic, I'd like to move on to your discussion of incident G9 which begins at page 75 of the English and page 142 of the B/C/S. And if we could go to page 148 of the B/C/S. You've made some assertions about the size of the craters of the 76-millimetre artillery shell craters or at least what were determined to be such at the time. And one of the things you do is you compare the crater in figure 92 which we can see on the top of the page with the crater in figure 93, the crater from the 82-millimetre mortar shell. Now, it's clear that you've made your determinations about the dimensions of these craters purely from photographs. It's common ground that these craters are no longer present on the ground. And you have -- you've made a comparison of the size -- this is at paragraph 102. You've made a comparison of the size of the 76-millimetre crater with a 82-millimetre mortar crater and you base that on the relative amounts of TNT in the two shells. And that's at footnote 397 and paragraph 102.1. Now, you would agree that a mortar is essentially an anti-personnel weapon. It's designed to fragment into small pieces and essentially kill people, whereas artillery shells are used for destroying structures and have a larger blast effect for that reason; right? And I would refer to -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Both the artillery projectiles that are produced as contact fuse variants and mortar projectiles have the same purpose. I say "contact fuse" which means that it's a projectile intended for destroying personnel with fragmentation effect. Now we have of course shaped charge, penetration, et cetera, et cetera. We're talking about the contact fuse projectile here, the TF projectile, which has the same purpose as the projectile which is produced for the 82-millimetre mortar as well as other mortars. It has a casing which through its fragmentation is intended for live personnel. This is an artillery projectile of a small calibre and small explosive charge and can in no way be used for blast effect. As I said, its main purpose is to be used for people and unprotected features.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. But you don't deny that the shells themselves have quite different properties. So, for example, I looked up the specks of the M70 shell, which the investigators determined was the shell fired in this case, and the entire round weighs 8.2 kilos, of which 5.2 kilos is the steel jacket. Whereas an 82-millimetre shell, the entire round weighs about 3 kilos and that includes the 680 grams of TNT. So the steel jacket is significantly or somewhat less than that. So do you agree that the steel jacket of the M70 would be significantly heavier and thicker than that of an 82-millimetre shell?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I have to ask you something. What you've just read out as the features of the projectile, are you sure about the weight of the jacket or is that the entire projectile? Because it is a one-piece projectile. So probably the weight of the casing itself was factored in. It would be -- it would not to be expected that what you've read out is correct I'm sorry to say that.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: You think what I've read out is -- sorry. You think what I've read out for the M70 artillery shell is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Okay. Could we have 65 ter --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just wait for the translation. I'm afraid we are missing something. Did you want to answer, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to say that this is a relatively small projectile and it is a one-piece projectile. What does it mean? It means that the charge or the filling is not separate. Rather, it is a one-piece, the casing and the filling form one piece. So the mass of the jacket indicated by the Prosecutor, she -- what she read out was the entire steel jacket comprising the casing and the jacket, you said that it was 7 to 8 kilos -- at any rate, I think it should be checked.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 25059A [Realtime transcript read in error "250598"], please. That should be 65 ter "25059A" rather than "8."

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, this is an extract from a JNA ammunition manual. If we could go to the next page in both languages. It has the technical data for the M70 shell which is the ammunition for the M48 B1 cannon, which again was the weapon determined to be the weapon in this case. And you can see it has the weight and length dimensions and it says the bullet jacket weighs 5.2 kilos and the entire round weighs 8.2 kilos; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's all right. I understood you to say that the jacket weighed 8 kilos. That's why I intervened.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Maybe there was a --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have to understand that through interpretation I hear steel parts being mentioned -- it's very difficult for me to grasp which of the figures that you mentioned relates to which feature. Can you please repeat your question so that I can give you an answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I did repeat my question and you did give me an answer, so I don't think I need to repeat it a third time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll receive the cover page and this page.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P6325.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now, just in terms of the dimensions and weight of this round it's, as I said, 8.2 kilos and is a little over 64 centimetres long. Now, this is the shell that you assert was --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, an intervention. It cannot be repeated that what comes to the point of impact is 8.2 kilos when it was already cleared up that this was not the case because the cartridge case will remain in the cannon --

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry, this is the accused giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't follow his point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The point of the matter is that Ms. Gustafson is repeating again that what is part of the impact is something that weighs 8.2 kilos. A moment ago we cleared up that the entire shell weighs 8.2 kilos and what impacts the site is something that weighs 5.8 kilos.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it's 5.2 kilos.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: I made no assertion of what impacted the site. That's totally inappropriate. This is -- these enumerable interventions make it virtually impossible.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, the dimensions of this round is 8.2 kilos and is a little over 64 centimetres long. This is the round that you claim on your theory was placed on the sidewalk in front of the shop and across from the flea market about 9.00 in the morning and then was detonated with a TNT charge. So I take it that you also take the position that this round would have had to have been detonated remotely and could you explain how that occurred on your theory?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to start from the beginning of your question again because I have to correct it. You said that it was my position that the projectile of a specific length and weighing 8.2 kilos was placed there, but no, that's not correct. Please. My position is that the projectile which was detached from its charge, so there is no case cartridge case, there is no charge, no filling, it was placed horizontally on the site of the explosion and activated with a Trotyl round. There is more than one piece of physical evidence that supports it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: There is no French translation. Shall we have a break. We'll resume at 1.17. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.47 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I just have one final question and then I'll hand the floor over to Mr. Gaynor --

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I just noticed that the witness never really got to complete her answer to the last question. She -- it was put to her that can you explain how the round could have been detonated remotely. She started to answer and then we took the lunch break. So I think it's only fair to give her a chance, if she wants to, to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Was it not a problem of translation? I think she completed her answer. I don't think -- no, no, no -- yes. Because -- ah, yes. We stopped because there was no French translation at the time. So probably she has to repeat her answer. Yes, thank you for the reminder. Probably you may need to put your question again, Ms. Gustafson.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: My previous question before the break, Ms. Subotic, was that I take it that this M70 artillery shell on your theory was detonated remotely and can you explain how that remote detonation took place? In other words, the person who detonated the shell was at some distance from the projectile. Can you explain how on your theory the shell was detonated?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say that at the beginning of your question you said shells 8.70 [as interpreted], I don't know what this relates to. That was what I received through interpretation. You probably wanted to say M70, 76-millimetres. When you first put that question, you said that it was a projectile weighing 8.2 kilogrammes. We have to clarify one thing on that score. This isn't the projectile that was activated; rather, the projectile that was activated on the site was detached from the cartridge case and its propellant -- its propelling charge, which is its component part. So it's a projectile without its charge which was most probably remotely activated with a TNT round. It was placed horizontally because that is what the physical evidence on the site indicates. There is one other piece of physical evidence that we registered, or rather, not we but the investigators did, which is that the fuse was retrieved outside of the crater far from the incident site some 20 metres, I believe, away from the centre. It was of course found lying laterally, and the interesting point is that it was found intact which means that it did not take part in the activation of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Now we're getting into something else. My question was about how this round was detonated --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: It's -- I understand your position that it was detonated with a TNT charge, but how was that TNT charge activated in order to explode the shell? Was it done with a timer? With a fuse? With a wire? How did that take place on your theory?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my view, it most probably happened with the use of a Trotyl bullet. What is it? It's a cube weighing 200 grams, I believe, in which a detonating primer is placed and that primer can be activated remotely.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: And how does that remote activation take place? Is it with a wire? How do you explain that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can take place in various ways. At this time I cannot go into a discussion around these technical details with you. As an expert in this field, I would have to have something that has been uncovered or retrieved in order for me to be able to give a proper answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. GUSTAFSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Subotic. That concludes my examination. I'll hand the floor over to Mr. Gaynor now.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Ms. Subotic. I'm going to --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm going to be asking you first about your modified air bombs report and then we're going to be discussing the Markale 1 incident and then we'll discuss Markale 2. For this first part I'd like you to keep your answers as short and concise as possible. It concerns fairly uncontroversial matters. Is that okay?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's all very well. I am just kindly asking you to wait for me to get the report that I need. I didn't know in which order you would take them.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Subotic, first of all, could you identify the ballistic parameters which affect the trajectory of any object flying through the atmosphere, whether it's a soccer ball or an American football or an air bomb or a rocket. Could you just give us a quick list of what those factors are.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a good question for me. Above all, the flight of any object, let's call it projectile shall we, will be affected primarily by the velocity with which the projectile will be launched into its flight. It will be affected by its shape in such a way that there are resistance coefficients, coefficients of thrust upwards, all those coefficients that will be the result of the resistance of the surroundings in which the projectile will fly. Of course the environment itself through which it will be flying will have an impact as well, through the density, its own density, the coefficients that we just mentioned, and the forces, the mass of the object that is flying. It will also be affected by of course the meteorological conditions that can be changeable. And if you want me to go into detail, there is a huge amount of factors that will have an impact on this, but they will not equally affect a football or a rocket. We didn't speak of the rocket at all here. It's a separate issue because it entails a huge number of parameters that will not be the ones that would apply to what you've mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, in respect of the meteorological conditions, you accept that air temperature, air pressure, air humidity are relevant? You can just say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We provide various columns in the firing tables that you've probably seen which relate to the adjustments made on launching, adjustments in relation to the basic tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And one must also take into account cross wind, head wind, and a tail wind?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course there are adjustments as per firing tables which have to do with wind. There are standards according to which these adjustments are made. They're given in the firing tables.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want you to address now a projectile which is launched from the ground with the aim of hitting a target also on the ground, essentially a surface-to-surface situation. Now, the factors which will affect where the projectile will land will include not just the factors you've already identified but possibly contained within your explanation we have to consider in particular the total force imparted on the projectile and the direction, both vertically and horizontally, that the force is imparted on the projectile.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I have not understood what you meant to say. Maybe it's a matter of interpretation, but this is how it was interpreted to me just so you know. Whether you should be clearer in your question. You said that the total force which acts on the direction both vertically and horizontally should be taken into account. I'm not sure what you implied by this; I don't understand it. So if you can please rephrase it or if the interpretation can be corrected. I cannot answer because I cannot locate it professionally within my area of expertise.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, when a projectile is fired from the ground, the end point of that projectile will depend on, among other things, the total force imparted on the projectile?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I have to distinguish whether we're talking about active/reactive projectile or a classic artillery projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Any --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But never mind. If we view them both from same position, as far as I have understood, you wanted to say that the place where it would land would begin on the initial velocity of the projectile. Was that what you meant?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And yes, the range also depends on the initial velocity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. And also the direction, both vertically and horizontally, in which the projectile is launched; correct? Those factors will affect where the projectile lands. It's essentially common sense.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, now I understand what you meant with this question. You mean that depending on the launching parameters which are determined at the launching, it depends where the projectile will land. Yes, if the parameters are taken according to the tables properly, then it's -- there is a high likelihood that it would fall at the intended position rather than it would not. Was that the thrust of your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, this is a really uncontroversial point I think at this point in my examination. The --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The difference in altitude between the firing point and the target point is also relevant; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, for an unguided projectile, that is to say a projectile without a guidance system based on laser or GPS technology, even minor differences in the direction in which it is pointed or in the force imparted on the projectile will have a quite significant difference in where it lands. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that depends on the projectile. The artillery projectiles are much less sensitive to all the parameters that you just listed, whereas the rocket-assisted projectiles are more sensitive simply because of the nature and characteristics of their flight. The deviations are never great if the errors are not great. If the errors are minor then the deviation is also minor. If the error is great, then the deviation is greater which is only logical.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Certainly if you're firing a rocket-assisted projectile, based on what you said, you would need to have precise firing tables in order to fire it with any degree of accuracy. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it is true for any projectile which is used in artillery, whether it's rocket artillery or classic artillery. Without firing tables, it's impossible to hit a target.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, if we could just turn to your report which is D3540, page 198 in your version and page 215 in the English version, we see a FAB-100 free-fall air bomb. Now, just two simple points here. Obviously an air bomb is designed to be dropped from the air and tested to be dropped from the air and to fall on its target at a near-vertical angle. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is launched from aircraft from the air, and you can see if you look at the second image to the right it has a parachute which opens after launching which slows down its flight and so that the aircraft could drop it from lower altitudes. And they land at a high angle because that's what they're like.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Right. And now what I'd like to show is page 199 -- it's numbered page 199 in the B/C/S version and it is page 216 in the English version. And that shows the kind of bomb that you've just been talking about which is a retarded FAB-100. Can we see the picture of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: English page?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes. I mentioned the parachute that -- as an element which is used for retarding during launching.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Sorry, we can just deal with the English version. The image we had was just fine. But basically we agree that the FAB-100 comes in both retarded and unretarded varieties. One is a free-fall and one is a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's confirm that we have the same and correct document. For me, I can't find page 216. And the English -- I think the document in the e-court doesn't have it either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We don't have figure. What we have is correct, what we have on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The photograph on the left is, in fact, the free-fall air bomb that I was discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The right --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The photograph of the bomb is the bomb that we have been discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's in B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, this appears on page -- paginated as page 215 in the English version that I'm -- that I have and this is the modified air bombs report of the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Could you direct the Registry to upload that page.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Apologies, it's page 210 in the e-court version. I've been working off the paper version. Apologies. Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The -- well, what we see on the right of the screen in front of you is a FAB-250 retarded -- if you look at the television screen in front of you is a FAB-250 retarded system.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The purpose of this discussion is simply to clarify both the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Left is about FAB-100 and right is FAB-250.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Left is the FAB-100 free-fall version and right is the FAB-250 retarded bomb version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So left page appears on what page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, in the English version, the page in the actual hard copy is page 215.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's upload English 215 in English version. I don't think we have that. This is page 215 what we have.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's paginated as page 215 the hard copy version that I have, which I believe I brought from e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I have 215 which is consistent with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But Judge Baird's version is -- seems to be identical to yours. So there's confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: What I have at page 216, the heading is FAB-100, not 250, FAB-100, M80, HE, and it begins like this: "FAB-250 M79 HE bomb is designed for safe and effective bombing ..." So the heading is misleading.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely, Your Honours. And I hadn't noticed that particular point. The other point is whether we have, in fact, the correct -- whether the hard version that His Honour Judge Baird and I are using is the same as the e-court version. So I'll look into that. This is certainly what we have been working off based on what the Defence has provided us.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: But we can continue our discussion, I think, Ms. Subotic. We agree at the very least that both the FAB-100 and the FAB-250 come in free-fall version on the one hand and in a retarded version on the other; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, the purpose of the retarded version, as you've described, is for the safety of the crew in the aircraft so that the aircraft is out of the danger zone before the detonation takes place?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the safety of the aircraft crew, yes, correct. In order to give the pilot enough time to fly away from -- or rather, it's the security of the crew when it's launched from a low altitude so that they could get away from the area that is affected by the blast.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Elsewhere in your reports you've referred to the existence of a FAB-275 modified aircraft system; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. FAB-275 was a development stage of the air bombs with liquid charge and in that stage there was a number of models --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the number of models.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the ground we did not find any traces of such explosions and they were destroyed at the end of the war, not even then but quite recently, 58 of the models which, as far as I know, were produced. I did not have the opportunity to see the results and I did not write in my report that there were such modified air bombs -- modified if we are talking about the rocket-assisted bombs. I suppose that that's what you meant in your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, we'll get to those in a minute. For the moment with the air bombs we've been discussing, clarify with a very brief answer, we agree they were unguided; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We agree that the free-fall and retarded varieties had different mass; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 117 -- I don't have the data about the retardation bombs, considering its mass, but I don't think that there needs to be some special difference in mass. The additional mass is just in the retardation mechanism, and apart from that it's an identical bomb. And in these 100-odd kilogrammes, the difference would be rather negligible. I mean, the manufacturer did not provide the data about the difference in mass.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps you can look at this over the weekend, but in the appendix of your report it's quite clear that for the FAB-250 retarded bomb its weight without the parachute system and fuses is 259.5 kilogrammes, and in the FAB-250 free-fall variety its weight without the fuses, because obviously there's no parachute system, is 240 kilogrammes.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, we can also agree that both the retarded and free-fall versions came in different lengths; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, yes, you're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, are you agreeing with my assertion about the lengths? They came in different lengths, right, free-fall and retarded?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. They may vary in length.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, we agree that the retarder system would have been designed and tested, we can agree probably extremely well tested, for an air-to-surface delivery only; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My point being --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean the product we are looking at now, I mean these bombs which are meant to be launched from aircraft which we're looking at now in this appendix, they were tested in view of the conditions under which they would be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That is to say they were designed and tested for air-to-surface delivery, not for surface-to-surface delivery; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. However, their design, if you look at them, does not deviate much from the design of a mortar shell because the design of a projectile is dictated primarily by the aerodynamic conditions under which such a projectile is to be used, that is to say the velocities with which it is moving so that this would be adapted to the conditions of minimum resistance during flight. This is the typical appearance of a subsonic projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, just taking one -- only one factor of difference between an air bomb and a mortar is that the propelling force for an air bomb is gravity and the propelling force for a mortar are the charges on the mortar. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is certainly evident, but the force of launching is not just -- the propelling force is not just gravity because the velocity is increased because of the flight of the aircraft. That's one thing. And also the propelling force does not affect the factors of flight, but rather the velocity. And the design is produced precisely by taking into account the speed of flight or the velocity of flight and it's obvious here that it is a subsonic projectile. For the conditions of the flight it does not matter what -- the propelling force is communicated, but what it -- its exact value is.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We'll move now to the characteristics of rockets. Now, I believe it's common ground that the air bombs were attached to different numbers of rockets depending on the configurations, and you have accepted that the air bombs were attached to rockets in configurations of one rocket, three rockets, and four rockets; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I analysed those types.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And you've accepted that at least the Grad 120-millimetre rocket was used with these air bombs; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the rocket engines which were used for the rocket artillery of the Grad systems were most often and almost always used in the incidents which we analysed.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I should correct my question. What we're actually talking about is the Grad 122-millimetre rocket; correct? I erroneously said "120-millimetre."

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, 122.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to go through a couple of uncontroversial assertions. Again, if you can keep your answers brief, please. The Grad 122-millimetre rocket has no guidance system; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It is designed to be fired from a tube or a barrel; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's designed to be launched from a barrel, the multi-barrel rocket-launcher. It can be fired as one or as a salvo.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say it's designed as such I mean that the entire rocket is designed as such, not just the rocket engine.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The -- when you say it's designed to be fired singly or in a salvo you accept that it's certainly not designed to be fired in a simultaneous fashion; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has this possibility if it's needed, but it's not -- look, let me repeat again. The design depends on the conditions of the flight and not on the manner of launching.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd like to --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you imply under the design the appearance of the rocket because aerodynamically we would imply that under design the appearance and its aerodynamic and dynamic configuration in relation with the tactical technical requirements.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask the Registrar, please, for 65 ter 25082, please. What's coming up on the screen in a moment is an extract from the report that you co-authored with Mr. Poparic which concerns inconsistencies which you believe to exist in the evidence of Mr. Zecevic and Mr. Higgs. And when it comes up, we could look at the third page, please. One language is all that's necessary. We could use the English.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [In English] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It will be on the screen in front of you in a minute.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, but I find it easier to look at my own document. Please tell me -- aha.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: It's page 64 in your version, Ms. Subotic. What we have on the screen in front of us, I think, is the top a Croatian multiple-barrel rocket-launcher and at the bottom a Czech multiple-barrel rocket-launcher. Both are designed and tested to fire 122-millimetre rockets; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, this system if you were to fire off ten rockets simultaneously, there is an extremely high danger that two or more of the rockets might collide in mid-flight; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Do you accept that these multiple-barrel rocket-launchers typically fire rockets in a salvo where there is a very short duration of time between the exit of each of the rockets from the rocket-launcher? Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, when we're talking about a salvo, it is fired simultaneously, and what you asked me previously is simply impossible. Because each rocket that is launched after the first one cannot catch up with it, aerodynamically there is no such possibility. That's why they cannot collide in mid-flight.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The very reason why these rocket-launchers are designed to fire in a salvo is to ensure that there is a distance between each rocket in the air. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The reason for launching salvos is actually to secure simultaneous covering of a much wider area which is targeted, because this is a fire support weapon. Like a howitzer, it's a weapon with which you fire over the heads of your troops during a war and you target a wide area at which the enemy is situated with his equipment or troops. And actually, the goal of launching a salvo is to cover a wide expanse of space which cannot be secured by single projectiles fired by the artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Okay. Let's start with some basics here. My idea of a salvo is not a simultaneous exit of rockets, but a consecutive exit of rockets from a multiple-barrel launcher system. When I say "consecutive," I mean you may fire off a relatively large number within two or three seconds. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's practically simultaneous launching.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That's exactly the point, it's not exactly simultaneous, but it takes place within a very short period of time. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's the tolerant field of this piece of equipment so no one hits one after another, but it is set --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Is it your evidence --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- on construction because the piece of equipment is constructed for this sort of action.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, is it your expert evidence that multiple-barrel rocket-launchers are designed to fire all of the rockets in the system at exactly the same moment, that is to say with complete synchronicity; is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the salvo consists of -- but look, the salvo can launch one row after another or everything simultaneously. That's a matter of choice. So they do not have to be launched at one single moment to a second, but it can be one row after another.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Let me put it this way: Are you -- have you ever seen or have -- physically or have you ever seen test data for any kind of device designed to ensure the precisely synchronous firing of rockets.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecutor please come closer to the microphone when speaking. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean the launching system, the ignition system? I've seen the entire system and I produced tables for the entire system for both Orkan and Organ as I've already stated. However, that special ignition device or launch device, I did not have to test it because that was not within the scope of my professional activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
