utterances.text: Right. Well, I'm going to put this to you that rockets are not designed to be fired simultaneously. They're designed to be fired in a salvo, which is to say consecutively, albeit with extremely short durations of time between the exit of each rocket from the MBRL?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we're discussing this all this time. This is what I told you to start with, didn't I?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So you'll agree with that assertion?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I already said at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now if we can move on, please, to the first page of the document which is on the screen in front of us, this is a page taken from the same report and it appears for your benefit, Ms. Subotic -- it appears just a few pages beforehand, it's page 62 in your version, Ms. Subotic. Now, if we just look at table 1 - we can focus in on table 1, please - you have set forth there the characteristics of four kinds of modified air bomb systems that you concede did exist. And I would like to draw your attention to a couple of aspects of it. First of all, in the extreme left column under the title rocket specifications at the fourth entry it says "warhead mass." Now, it's quite clear, isn't it, that by "warhead," you mean the actual air bomb itself; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, if we move down to propulsion number of motors, it's only fair to say that there is, in fact, a typo there. If we go across to the fourth entry where it says 4 GRAD under the column which is headed RFAB-250-3, what you probably meant there was 3 GRAD. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the column number? Is it column 3, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... go to the column on the extreme right which is the column for the FAB-250 with three rockets --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, under the propulsion number of motors you have 4 GRAD. Obviously what you meant was 3, wasn't it? I think it's just a typo.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Third column from left to right, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you are looking at the same document. Could you look at the monitor.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I am actually looking at the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you -- if we could put the cursor on the 4 GRAD Mr. Gaynor is referring to. Do you recognise the cursor on the monitor, Ms. Subotic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Whether that 4 GRAD should read "3 GRAD."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see, yes, yes, of course. You are right. I was looking at a wrong line indicating the mass. So yes, the number is wrong. It should be 3 GRAD, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I thank you for the correction. It is, indeed, a typo. I was looking at the mass. There was no inconsistency there so I didn't really follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now if you --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript. On line 1 it doesn't say that it is a typo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, just look at the line which has the total impulsive force -- or total impulse in Newtons, I believe. Do you see it?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And do you accept that the total impulsive force is obviously different if it's propelled by one rocket, three rockets, or four rockets?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, yes. That's why the number of rockets is increased.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And you accept that given that we're dealing with rockets of different numbers and air bombs of different weights, that the total mass of each modified air bomb in each of these four varieties is different. Do you accept that? You can do the addition if you want.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Neither you nor I know whether we were dealing with bombs of different masses or whether they were all the same. So that part is something that we cannot take into account as something exact. That's our entry assumption or starting assumption. When it comes to different total masses, as a result of changes in the number of rockets, of course that's correct because each rocket has its own mass.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, given that we agree that there was a different combination of mass and propulsive force for each of these four varieties of modified air bombs, can we also agree that the ballistic properties for each of these four varieties is different?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For all these four varieties, three engines, one engine, four engines or FAB with three or four engines, yes, the ballistic characteristics of those projectiles, i.e., these rockets are different which means that each of the projectiles in different columns equipped with the number of rockets that is stated in the table results in the different ballistic characteristics of each and every such projectile. I agree with you on that, and that's what I've already stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And can we agree that your table does not, in fact, get into the difference between free-fall FAB-100 and retarded FAB-100, nor does it address the difference between free-fall FAB-250 and retarded FAB-250. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel kindly get closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: My apologies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you allow me to consult my previous expertise? --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer -- before I answer your question, do you know what this is all about? This is the stabilisation of a projectile. We're talking about intervention on a projectile when it was modified, i.e., the fuse was taken out from the back and rocket engines were mounted instead with their own stabilisers. Therefore, we don't have any proof that that was indeed done. That's why I wanted to see what we found in the incidents and what those stabilisers and remains looked like.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic, we'll get to the process of attaching the rockets to the bombs in a few minutes. Right now I think we can agree that this table here makes no mention of retarder systems; correct? There's no mention of a parachute, any effect of a parachute on the ballistic characteristics of the projectile; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The parachute system is not mentioned for a simple reason, that system would have to be eliminated for such a table. That's why it is not mentioned. It is not that the system exists or doesn't exist. It doesn't exist, that's why it's not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No problem, but we do agree that the presence or absence of a parachute on a modified air bomb or on an unmodified air bomb certainly has an enormous effect on where that bomb is going to land; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know, in technical sciences, we insist on figures. So when you say "enormous," I don't know what that implies, what size or dimension or length. So could you please be more specific and can we please use understandable dimensions. Only in that case will I be able to agree with you or not. Normal [as interpreted] is when the projectile falls in the centre of its expected trajectory. We consider that as being normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Let me just put one example to you and we'll move on because we're pressed for time. In your report you have taken a base-line figure of 6.000 metres for the distance of the trajectory travelled by modified air bombs; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Transcript, please. This may have an impact on the further course of discussion. On line 25 the doctor didn't say "normal" but "enormous." When it falls at half the trajectory. So she didn't use the word "normal" but "enormous," and she said what would be an "enormous" size or parameter.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I think the accused is aware that the transcript does undergo revision each and every day of trial. I think we can afford to continue. Yes. By "revision," I mean revision after the court day is over.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Ms. Subotic --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wanted to answer your question with regard to the 6.000 metres. You wanted to ask me something with this regard and then we were interrupted. You said that in my report I took 6.000 metres as the distance travelled by a projectile before reaching the place of an incident. I have to say the following: Yes, we did, and that refers to the assessment of precision and the assessment of the deviation from the possible target place. Why is that? There was no situation in which we had an opportunity, technical opportunity, to exactly determine the place of launch. That's why we took into account an average range or distance as our bench-mark for analysis. That's what we did and I hope that this is how you understood it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And for the benefit of the record that appears at paragraph 151 of your report. Now, just very quickly on the parachute issue. If this chute --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No need to look at it right now. If the chute were to deploy at 3.000 metres in one instance and if it were to deploy at 5.000 metres in a second instance, do you accept that the landing point in the first instance would be quite considerable distance away from the landing point in the second example?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I did not understand the interpretation. Did you ask me the following, please, bear with me. If the target or the targeted distance was 6.000 metres, then you believe that there would be one deviation from the landing point, probable deviation. And when it is 3.000 metres, the deviation point is different and that those deviations would differ. Is that what you asked me?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No, we'll get to your calculation of deviations later. I'm simply saying that if the retarder system were to deploy in one example after 3.000 metres and in the second example at 5.000 metres, obviously, I suggest, the landing location in each of those two examples of the projectile would be entirely different?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I ask, I really don't understand. Are we talking about bombs launched from surface with retarding -- retarder mechanisms? Because this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you leave it to Ms. Subotic. If she doesn't understand, she will ask for clarification. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is exactly what I wanted to ask you. Are we talking about air bombs launched from aircraft and the deployment of retarder systems or something else? I didn't understand. You are -- you have mentioned retarder systems; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'll put this to you one final time because I'm pressed for time. If you were to deploy, fire, launch modified air bomb with a retarder system in it and if the retarder system, which is to say a small parachute, were to open after 3.000 metres, that projectile would land somewhere. In the second example you take a similar model, the parachute opens not after 3.000 metres but after 5.000 metres, it would land in location B. Surely you accept that the distance between location A and location B would be quite different?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know what? This is such a hypothetical situation. I don't see any technical justification for it. On the one side we have equipment that should carry it as far as possible and then we deploy retarder systems at our own discretion. This is such a hypothetical question that it's impossible to answer. It's an impossible situation. I don't see the purpose of somebody attaching three rockets to a bomb in order to propel it as far as possible following the norms of dynamics, and then they will deploy a parachute that will retard it, that will make it deviate in an unknown direction. This is not the kind of research that we do. We do the research that we discussed when we started talking and that's for air-to-surface delivery. That's when we use those retarder systems. In any case, in none of the incidents did we find anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to turn to an appendix to your report and it appears on what is on the hard copy version page 221 in English, and on the hard copy version in B/C/S it is page 205. And it shows a thrust diagram for the Grad 122-millimetre rocket motor.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. Paragraph number?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: In your version, Ms. Subotic, it's page 205.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now -- we have it now. If we could turn it on its side. I think -- that's excellent. If we could get the English up as well. This shows the consumption, really, of the propellant within the rocket; right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak slowly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Doctor, Ms. Subotic, could you repeat and speak slowly. And I have to note this is English page 212.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In attachment to my expertise there is a thrust diagram for the Grad 122-millimetre rocket engine and it was obtained on the testing table. This was a result of static research, not dynamic research. There is a certain difference in the function of this thrust in dynamic conditions as opposed to static research. But this is correct enough for our purpose for designing firing tables, which is why we do not test such assets under dynamic conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And it's right, isn't it, the propulsive force in a Grad rocket is provided by propellant in that rocket and the propellant is used up in about 1.8 seconds; correct? That's what this graph tells us.

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 1.8, yes, that's correct, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to move in a moment - and we can keep this on the screen for a moment - to the process of attaching rockets to the air bomb. Now, in a minute we're going to see a diagram of an air bomb to which are attached four rockets. Now, would you agree with the proposition that it is absolutely vitally important to ensure the accuracy of that system that each of the four rockets should be ignited at exactly the same moment?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Because let's say one of the rockets were to ignite 0.4 of a second after the other three, it would still be burning 0.4 of a second after the other three had stopped burning; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: That would obviously have a huge effect on the stability of the projectile, sending it off in an unknown -- possibly a huge squiggly trajectory through the sky?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course not. First of all, it wouldn't be unstable. It would just receive another additional impulse that would increase dispersion. Stability is not determined by the rocket thrust because that would be disturbance. Lunas rocket were distinguished. So it is not provided by the work of the rocket engines. The stability of the engines of this kind slightly rotating projectiles is determined based, or rather, as the type of statically stable projectiles, we have statically stable projectiles and dynamically stable projectiles. This is a statically stable projectile which by the position of the resulting thrust force with regard to the centre of mass is what determines its stability. The stability is not jeopardised with this. There is just one thing that remains and that is an impulse that impacts dispersion but not in the sky, that's for sure, if that is what you said. I don't -- the interpreter translated your words as a projectile swaying through the sky and I'm just returning your words back to you. I suppose that this is what you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I want to put it to you that after -- with 0.4 seconds left in the fuel tank, if you like, the impulsive force being driven on the modified air bomb system by that one rocket that is still going is by your own graph 25.000 Newtons decreasing down to 0. Do you accept that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is indeed the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And you're suggesting that with one engine firing on 25.000 Newtons and the other three engines silent and quiet, that that would not have much of an effect on the trajectory of that projectile?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I have already told you, it would have an impact on the increase in dispersion, but you omitted a fact that you have already repeated several times. That projectile is easily managed with just one rocket engine because we're talking about a projectile with four rocket engines and it weighs about 250 kilogrammes. Just one -- if only one rocket engine could guide it to go where we want, we would not fix four to it. First and foremost, it's impulse that has its impact on the dispersion, but it cannot do what you mentioned in your question. It cannot have exceptionally unexpected effects or deviations or -- I don't know how else to put it. In any case, it does have an effect, but not as significant as it seems to you. Let me assure you, if one rocket engine sufficed, we would not attach four to it. I mean us -- I don't mean that I ever attached a rocket engine to a projectile. I mean us as a profession. We wouldn't advise that to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Right. Well, let's go on to the attachment of one rocket to an air bomb system. Could I call up, please, video P5982. And if we could play the video from the beginning until 35 seconds, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: We can stop, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, first of all, let me just note for the record that Your Honours have already seen this video and you did ask for some information as to where the Prosecution got it from. I have that information for you now. The video was provided to the ICTY Berko Zecevic when he was an expert witness in the case against Dragomir Milosevic. And according to Mr. Zecevic at this part of the video there is a 1 minute, 30 second clip showing the 21st sabotage unit of the VRS using a modified air bomb launcher during the military operation Grude 77, date unknown. Now, Ms. Subotic, can we agree that this appears to show the attachment of a single rocket to an air bomb?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And what we're looking at on the frame which is visible in front of you at the moment is a launch system which was used to launch the modified air bomb using a rail delivery system as opposed to, for example, a barrel delivery system. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean the rails from which the rockets are launched?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. You accept that what's in front of us is --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the three-rail construction, and it's rail launch. The rockets have their own tails that dovetail the rails as you see them, and in this position they are in a stable orientation in the direction of their launch. So this isn't something that would be in a free fall.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You saw in your -- in that video soldiers who appeared to be screwing the rocket from which the warhead had presumably been removed into the base of the air bomb; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are rocket engines and they are produced the way they are. The warheads have not been taken off them. The rocket engines are manufactured especially in the way they appear here. It's a specific -- it's a separate product, you see, there's no need to take it off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What has been left out is that the witness said that they are perfectly centred in -- as they are positioned on these rails and what is meant is the tails of the rockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. That brings us to a very important point. It's extremely important not only that the screw thread at the top of the rocket should match the screw thread at the bottom of the air bomb but also that it should be precisely in the centre of the air bomb. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do agree with you that it is necessarily so that they have to be at the centre. We saw it on the case involving three engines that there was a band which was there to make sure that it is at the centre, and here yes there is some sort of a screw-on system. And the coaxiality between the rocket force and the projectile itself is very important.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: And can we agree that the ultimate location of the rocket after it is fired and it has struck the ground at the other end will depend of course on the angle of elevation of the rails and the direction in which the rails are pointing?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The position of the rails must be set according to the parameters of the flight that are necessary for the desired range and direction. This is the artillery system, you know. This is what is inherent to artillery systems, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: You will agree that the longer the rails, the further the bomb will travel as a general proposition?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The bomb will fly further depending on the rocket propulsion it has within. That's the range, and of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- it is from the conditions of -- it is the stable launching that will determine it and not the range.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: All other things being equal, do you agree that the length of the rails has an effect on the distance travelled by the projectile which is launched from those rails?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it has nothing to do with it. Absolutely nothing, believe me.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: So your evidence is that if I were to launch a modified air bomb from a launch system with a rail of 4 metres long, it would land at precisely the same point as if I were to launch the modified air bomb from a rail system which was 25 metres long? Is that your evidence?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is my evidence. However, there is a small departure from it. When we -- there would be a deviation in terms of what is the classic dispersion, and I did say a moment ago that the length of the rails will have an impact on the precision because the launch will be stable, as I said. So, for instance, you could have 25 metres-long rails and this would have no bearing on the range if on that bomb you had the same rocket engine. So in other words, the length of the rails does not have an influence on the range.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Except on the dispersion of the initial impulses.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, it looks like we've reached agreement that the length of the rails will have an impact on the precision?

utterances.speaker: ZORICA SUBOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the precision, but this has no bearing on the range whatsoever. It is on this basis that the length of the -- length and width of the rail is defined, on the basis that it has no bearing on the range.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Well, if your position is that the range -- the distance travelled by the projectile and the precision of the projectile are totally separate concepts - I'll let you stay with that position?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Perhaps I can ask the Registrar to bring up 65 ter 24355, please. We're going to be looking at a couple of photographs here. For the record, these are photographs taken by ICTY investigator Todd Cleaver on the 19th of April, 1996, in Vogosca in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As to your explanation about the previous video, I didn't follow your explanation, in that Mr. Zecevic provided this to the ICTY. Does it mean he filmed this?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: No. Thank you for the opportunity to clarify. I believe this video is independently available on the internet. The original part of this is from a documentary entitled "Komsije 2," produced by Pavle Vranjican and Ivica Pandza, Orkan, in Zagreb on a date unknown. It contains footage of many different events, including events relating to the Krajina Serbs, Serb forces in Croatia, actions by what are described as the Mujahedin in Bosnia, and events relating to Operation Storm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Now, the picture in front --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have the floor for a brief moment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Subotic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. I don't know how much time we have left, if we have a lot of time left can I have just a five-minute break. How long will the session last? I don't mind, it's just that I need a five-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We're going to adjourn very soon but --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In that case, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have one thing to raise in private session in your absence. Probably you could be excused for five minutes. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. Am I to understand that this is part of the documents that have been redacted from the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Robinson's absolutely right about that. These couple of pages did fall within a part of a report that Your Honours have ordered the redaction of. Now, I would submit that they do identify some areas where the Prosecution and Defence do have common grounds, that these four different kinds of modified air bombs at the very least did exist and also has a couple of helpful pictures about multiple-barrel rocket-launchers. So we're quite happy to submit -- I think it's just four pages for Your Honours for that reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Witness can be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't mind admitting the document, but we want to keep open the option of tendering additional pages from the redacted material during Mr. Poparic's testimony because whether or not there is other material that would be relevant to these pages that have now been referred to, we can look at that when we -- if and when it's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we leave it for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. President, as you've helpfully reminded me, I did mean to tender -- yes, that -- excuse me. I'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The photograph --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, I was going to ask you about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In line 1, page 107, what is recorded is quite the opposite. The witness said that the rails are designed in such a way so as not to have impact on precision and not range, and I would really object to the playing of a video which has nothing to do with my army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If I may respond. Purpose of the video was to raise a discussion about the importance of attaching a rocket to an air bomb and the effect of various characteristics of the launch system and the importance of precision in all those aspects. So I would suggest even if other armies around the world had been using modified air bombs, it wouldn't make a great deal of difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The video was already in evidence. But for the transcript, do you confirm what Mr. Karadzic pointed out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's what I said. It does not have any effect on range, but rather on precision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. By now, albeit symbolically, as you have put it, extended our sitting by 15 minutes. But I'm now wondering whether there's a point of further extension and whether there's -- we should extend next week's sitting at all. Where are we and where do we stand?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, I don't think it's necessary to extend the sittings. We're still taking steps to see if one witness from next week might be rescheduled, but in any event I think we can proceed with the normal schedule.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who will be the first witness next week Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Uscumlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So Ms. Subotic's evidence will be interposed by him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the circumstances, do you have more questions or should we adjourn for the week?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'm quite happy to break at this stage, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll do that. Next week we'll resume on Tuesday at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 21st day of May, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
